idiom_name: shared operator carrier (mixin base / protocol with defaults / module mixin / type class) plus one primitive operation per family member
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: identify the family of types that share one operator vocabulary, put the derived operators in a single carrier (a base class template parameterised on the family member, a protocol with default implementations, a module or trait mixin, or a type-class instance), and require each member to implement only the primitive operation(s) the carrier is written in terms of - equality plus one ordering relation, or the compound arithmetic primitive. Let the language's own lookup find the operators by the operands' types (argument-dependent lookup of in-class friends, protocol conformance, module inclusion, an implicit or given instance), so no namespace-level or per-call-site declaration is necessary. Nothing in this approach is specific to C++.
code_sketch:
carrier OperatorFamily<Member>:        # template / protocol / module / trait
    op_a(x, y) = derived_from(primitive)
    op_b(x, y) = derived_from(primitive)

member Money of the family:
    primitive(x, y) -> bool | int      # the only operation a member implements

lookup by operand type:                # ADL / conformance / include / implicit
    Money(x) op_a Money(y)             # found with no scope-level declaration
pitfalls: Putting the derived operators in the carrier and also duplicating them per member creates two definitions that drift apart; the carrier must stay the single source of truth.
A carrier that applies to every type - an unbounded template, a universal protocol, an implicit instance in global scope - silently changes the behaviour of unrelated code; restrict it to the family.
